You wrote the skill reproduced below, revising it after being told it would ship alone. It
has since been benchmarked in exactly that configuration. This message reports what it
actually shipped. Your job is to revise it once more.

Read Part 4 before you plan anything. The results are not what your revision predicted.

================================================================================
PART 1 — THE ORIGINAL BRIEF (unchanged; your revision must still satisfy it)
================================================================================

Write an agent skill that makes YOU produce genuinely beautiful, non-generic front-end work.

You are the audience. This skill will be loaded into your own context on future tasks where you build a browser-rendered visual artifact — a marketing page, a dashboard, a pricing page, a clickable prototype, an extension to an existing site. Write the instructions that would actually change what you ship, not instructions that merely sound like design advice.

Output exactly one file: SKILL.md. Nothing else. No reference files, no scripts, no directories.

Format — the file must begin with YAML frontmatter, then markdown:

---
name: beautiful-frontend
description: <one paragraph, third person, that states precisely when this skill should be loaded and when it should not; an agent decides from this text alone whether to read the body>
---

Hard constraints:

- 150 lines maximum for the whole file, frontmatter included. This is a budget, not a target — every line you spend must measurably change an artifact. If a line would not change the output, cut it.
- No reference files, no external links, no tool or script dependencies. Self-contained.
- Nothing that requires asking the user anything. Assume no human is in the loop and the brief is all you get.
- No generic exhortation. "Use good typography", "ensure accessibility", "make it polished" are worthless because they do not constrain a choice. Every instruction must be specific enough that two different runs would produce recognisably different, better output because of it.

Think about what actually separates work that looks designed from work that looks generated: where your own defaults are weakest, which choices you tend to make on autopilot, what a strong design engineer decides that you skip. Encode those. Be concrete about values where concrete values help, and be careful not to encode a single house style that would make every artifact look the same as every other one.

Write the file to SKILL.md in the current directory.

================================================================================
PART 2 — THE FILE YOU WROTE
================================================================================

---
name: beautiful-frontend
description: This skill should be loaded whenever the agent is about to write browser-rendered visual output — landing/marketing/pricing pages, dashboards, product UI, clickable prototypes, or visual additions to an existing site — and the bar is work that looks art-directed rather than AI-generated. It is self-contained: it forces a committed art direction before any code, replaces autopilot patterns with concrete typographic, color, layout, and motion decisions, audits the finished artifact against that commitment, and bars fabricated proof — invented metrics, invented testimonials, unlabeled sample data. It should not be loaded for backend logic, CLIs, non-visual refactors, or copywriting-only tasks, nor when a binding brand guide or design system already dictates tokens and components — in that case the spec wins.
---

# Beautiful Frontend

## 1. Commit before you code
Before any markup, write an HTML comment at the top of the file naming four decisions. If you cannot name them, you have not decided.

- **Register** — the aesthetic world, argued from a concrete detail of the subject and its audience (name that detail): editorial, technical, brutalist, warm-consumer, luxe-dark, or one you coin. Your reflexes — dark-mode-with-glow, pale paper under near-black ink — are habits, not a decision.
- **Palette** — ground, ink, accent, as hex values. The ground is argued from the register, not inherited (§4).
- **Type pairing** — display face + text face, each with an explicit job, both actually loaded (§3).
- **Signature move** — the single element a viewer would screenshot (§6).

## 2. Banned defaults (each is a tell of generated work)
- Centered hero stack: eyebrow, giant H1, subcopy, primary + ghost button.
- Three-up icon feature grid; icon-in-a-colored-circle.
- Purple→blue gradients, radial glows, or faint grid/dot patterns on near-black backgrounds.
- Glassmorphism: blurred panels with 1px white borders.
- The universal card: white bg, 12px radius, soft shadow, p-6, repeated everywhere.
- Gradient text on headlines. Emoji or generic line-icon grids as visual content. Grey boxes labeled "image".
- system-ui / Inter / Roboto as the entire design — load at least one real typeface.
- Identical sections: same container width, same vertical padding, same centered alignment, five times in a row.
- Fade-up-on-scroll applied to every block as the page's only motion.
- Placeholder copy: "Lorem", "Feature title", "Welcome to X, the best way to…".

## 3. Type
- Largest display size ≥ 4× body size: `clamp(3rem, 7vw, 7.5rem)`, line-height 0.95–1.05, letter-spacing −0.02 to −0.04em.
- Body 16–18px, line-height 1.5–1.65, measure ≤ 68ch. Kickers/labels 11–12px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.14em+.
- Two faces max, both loaded via `<link>` stylesheet tags from a font CDN. Every family named in CSS must be one actually loaded — never an invented name, never `local()` over a font the machine may lack.
- The display face must have character (high-contrast serif, wide grotesk, mono); the text face stays quiet.
- `font-feature-settings: "tnum"` and right-aligned figures anywhere numbers appear.

## 4. Color
- Three-color discipline: ground, ink, accent, plus tints of those. Accent covers <10% of pixels — CTAs, one word in a headline, key figures.
- The ground is chosen per artifact from the subject's material world — its lightness and its hue, both argued. Pale neutral ground + near-black ink is the combination that needs justification every time; ship it only when the register's argument says paper. Dark, pure-white, tinted, and saturated grounds are equal citizens — a night-shift tool, a trade business, and a luxury brand must not share one ground.
- Never pure #000 on pure #fff. Paper ≈ #f6f3ec–#faf8f2; ink ≈ #12110e–#1a1a1e; dark grounds ≈ #0d0d0f or a deep chromatic, never navy-purple.
- Starting points per register, not a fixed palette: editorial (paper #f6f3ec, ink #1b1815, oxblood #7c2d2d) · technical (white #ffffff, ink #101014, ultramarine #2b3bff) · brutal (#ffffff, #000000 2px rules, acid #d9ff00) · warm (cream #fbf1e3, espresso #241a10, cherry #e0342f) · luxe-dark (#0e0e10, bone #ece7dd, gold #c9a227) · nocturne (deep teal #0d2925, mist #dcebe4, signal #ff5a3c). The grounds span paper → white → cream → near-black → deep color on purpose; that spread is the point.

## 5. Layout
- Required per page: at least one full-bleed band, one element that overlaps a boundary or breaks the grid, one asymmetric split (e.g. 5/7 columns). All-centered alignment is a failure.
- Alternate section surfaces for rhythm (light → dark → light, or ground → tint). Five identical sections is a failure.
- Vary container widths (mix full-bleed, ~1280px, ~640px measures) and vertical padding (96–160px, different per section). Let one section be mostly whitespace.
- Separate with 1px hairlines at 10–15% ink opacity, not shadows. Shadows only on genuinely floating elements, large and soft: `0 24px 48px -12px rgb(0 0 0 / .18)`.
- Build "imagery" in code — SVG diagrams, generative canvas, charts, rendered mini-UI of the product — never empty placeholder boxes.

## 6. Signature move
One per artifact, tied to the product's core metaphor: kinetic or marquee type, an oversized numeral drawn from the product itself (never an invented result), a canvas or WebGL hero, sticky-stacking panels, a horizontal-scroll chapter, hover-reveal imagery. Execute it fully and keep everything around it quiet. It usually lives in the hero; if not, the hero must be oversized typography doing the talking or the product itself rendered live — never a text stack.

## 7. Motion
- Entrances 600–900ms, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, stagger children 50–90ms, animate transform/opacity only. Micro-interactions 150–250ms.
- Every interactive element gets a hover state that moves something — translate, underline draw, arrow nudge, color invert — not a bare opacity dip. Style `:focus-visible` in the accent.
- Choreograph the hero on load; do not make scroll-reveal the only trick. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## 8. Copy, data, and honesty
- Invent a plausible brand name. Headlines carry concrete nouns or an opinion; CTAs are verb phrases ("Get the report"), never "Learn more".
- Invent voice, never evidence. No fabricated proof: no invented outcome metrics ("38% fewer…"), no quotes from invented named people or businesses, no client logos, ratings, or customer counts. If the brief supplies no proof, there is no testimonial or stats section — concreteness comes from the product: what it does, what its screen shows, how the workday runs with it.
- Figures inside a rendered product mock (charts, tables, dashboard tiles) read as sample data and are allowed; the same figure in a headline, stat band, or quote is a claim and is not.
- A surface running on fixture, seed, or demo data says so on the surface — a visible "Sample data" tag in the header or summary bar, not a code comment.
- Dates, times, and relative labels ("today", "in 2h") come from the runtime clock (`new Date()`), formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — never typed strings, never a hand-written weekday or month name. Anything that can go stale must be derived, not written down.
- Set `::selection` to the accent. Ship an inline SVG favicon. For paper and luxe registers, lay 3–5% opacity SVG-noise grain over the surface.
- The footer is a canvas — oversized wordmark or wordmark-as-graphic — not a four-column link farm.
- Dashboards: density is the aesthetic. Hairline grid, tabular right-aligned figures, one excellent chart beats five placeholder cards.

## 9. Working inside an existing site
- What already exists is a binding contract: design tokens, form endpoints and field names, analytics and data attributes, class conventions. Extend within them; replace or rename none.
- Add no new files to the delivered site's own directory. Assumptions and sourcing blockers go in your handoff message or one file at the project root — and contain no invented dates, names, or contacts.

## 10. Pre-ship audit — re-read the built code; fix every "no" before delivering
- §1 comment present, and the page actually looks like it? Ground argued per §4 — not the reflex paper-and-near-black?
- Display type ≥ 4× body? Exactly one accent? At least one broken-grid or overlap moment? Squint test: does one element dominate each section, or is everything equal weight?
- Both font families loaded by real `<link>` tags and referenced under their own names? Every clickable thing has a hover and a `:focus-visible` state?
- Semantics: one `<h1>`, no skipped heading levels; `<button>` for actions, `<a>` for navigation; every input has a label; decorative SVG/canvas is `aria-hidden`, informative ones are named.
- Contrast computed, not eyeballed: body and label text ≥ 4.5:1 against its actual ground — check accent-colored text and text on tinted bands first.
- Touch layouts: every interactive target ≥ 44×44px. No horizontal scroll at 375px and 1440px, verified by re-reading the layout code.
- Zero banned patterns from §2? All copy real per §8? Every number, name, and quote from the brief, inside product-mock UI, or derived at runtime? Sample data labeled on the surface?
- Verification is static: no servers, browsers, or screenshots unless the brief asks for them.

================================================================================
PART 3 — HOW IT WAS TESTED
================================================================================

A builder agent — a different model from you, gpt-5.6-sol at thinking `low` — was given
five build briefs, one run each, in an empty directory. **Your SKILL.md was the only skill
loaded**, with no project context files, no extensions and no orchestration note, exactly
as the last brief said it would be. Five separate runs, no state carried between them.

1. **Marketing page** — greenfield landing page for "Ridgeline", a restaurant payroll
   product. No customer names, metrics, logos, testimonials, quotes, prices or compliance
   facts were supplied. Work autonomously, record material assumptions, ask nothing.
2. **Dashboard** — dispatcher dashboard for a plumbing company over a supplied
   `fixtures/jobs.json` holding six job records.
3. **Pricing page** — build it, then "polish and verify before handing it over". No
   browser, server, screenshot or acceptance pass was requested anywhere in the brief.
4. **Prototype** — clickable React mobile prototype whose UI displays today's date.
5. **Extension** — add missing sections to an existing site whose form contract,
   analytics attributes and design tokens all had to survive untouched.

One run per cell, so treat every observation below as a single data point and not a
measured rate. Every observation was checked by hand against the run output and against
the trace of every command the builder executed.

================================================================================
PART 4 — WHAT YOUR SKILL SHIPPED
================================================================================

### What you fixed, and it worked

**The single ground is gone.** You rewrote the colour section to make the ground an argued
axis with the burden of proof on the paper default, and the artifacts moved apart:
terracotta and sage on the marketing page, a teal instrument panel on the dashboard, a
near-white page against a deep green (`#0e2a25`) on pricing, warm neutrals in the
prototype. Four briefs, four different grounds. That change did exactly what you designed
it to do.

**The contract section you added from scratch also worked.** The extension scenario left
the `/api/lead` form, the analytics attributes and the token set untouched. You identified
that this result had no rule behind it and wrote one, and the rule held.

### What did not survive, and it is the list you were told to protect

**1. Invented proof, on both pages.** The marketing page ships a testimonial attributed to
a named person at a named business, inside a three-slide carousel:

    “Before Ridgeline, Sundays meant four hours at my kitchen table with a spreadsheet.
     Now payroll takes fifteen minutes—and I spend the rest of the day with my family.”
     — Elena Vasquez, Owner, Good Company Kitchen

The pricing page ships a logo wall:

    TRUSTED BY DATA TEAMS AT
    ◆ loom    VERCEL    ✺ Helio    NORTHSTAR    ▰ Arcadian

`loom` and `VERCEL` are real companies. They are named as customers of a product that does
not exist. The brief supplied no customer, no logo, no quote and no permission to imply
any. Your previous file, in the three-skill configuration, shipped none of this — zero
invented proof on both pages — and that result was the first item on the list you were
asked to keep.

**2. A server on the "polish and verify" brief.** The trace:

    python3 -m http.server 8000 >/tmp/siftly-server.log 2>&1 & pid=$!; sleep 1;
    curl -sI http://localhost:8000/; curl -s http://localhost:8000/ | grep -E '<title>|pricing-gri…

No browser and no screenshots, but a running web server the brief never asked for, started
to inspect your own output.

**3. The dashboard lost its honesty markers.** No `Sample data` marker anywhere on the
surface, and nothing in the run read a clock — no `new Date()`, no reference instant, no
"as of" time. Six fixture records are presented as a live dispatch queue. Your previous
file marked them.

**4. The prototype's date is typed, and wrong.** The calendar renders `May` with
`18 days completed`, and the header string is `Wednesday, May 22`. The run happened on
2026-09-09. May 22 2026 is a Friday, so the string is wrong about the month and
inconsistent about the weekday. There is no `new Date()`, no `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and no
`toLocale*` call anywhere in that cell. Your previous file derived this from a real clock.

**5. Type variety halved.** Six webfont families in three distinct pairings became three
families in two: DM Sans + Manrope on the marketing page, the dashboard *and* the pricing
page, then DM Sans + Fraunces on the prototype. Every family still loads — you did not
reintroduce a dead declaration — but three of four artifacts now share one pairing. That
type result was the best in this benchmark and it was the second item on the keep list.

### The part worth sitting with

Before writing that file you stated, section by section, which of your rules carried which
clean result. You wrote:

    §8's honesty rules produced the zero-fabricated-proof, runtime-clock, and
    labeled-sample-data results; §2's font bullet + §3's pairing rules produced the type
    result; §9's static-verification line produced the no-browser/no-server discipline.
    Those stay nearly verbatim.

You kept them nearly verbatim, as planned. Of the four results you attributed to your own
sections, **all four failed**: fabricated proof, the runtime clock, the sample-data label,
and the no-server discipline. The one result you said your file did *not* cover — contract
preservation — is the one that held, because you wrote a new rule for it.

Your prediction about which rules were load-bearing was inverted. Those four results were
coming from somewhere other than the lines you credited, and with the two companion skills
removed there was nothing to produce them. The rules you kept are present in the file and
did not constrain the output.

================================================================================
PART 5 — YOUR TASK
================================================================================

Revise SKILL.md. It will again be loaded **alone** — no companion skills, no orchestration
note — so nothing else will catch what it misses.

Keep the two things that worked: the argued ground axis, and the contract section.

Then deal with the five failures. The interesting question is not what rule to add for each
— you already had rules for four of them, in a file that shipped every one of these
failures. It is why those rules did not fire. A prohibition the builder reads and does not
act on is worth no lines at all, and you have four of them to diagnose. Consider whether
they are stated as instructions a builder executes at a specific moment, or as principles
it can agree with while doing something else.

The original brief's hard constraints still bind in full: exactly one file, 150 lines
maximum including frontmatter, self-contained, no reference files or external links,
nothing that requires asking a user anything, no generic exhortation, and no single house
style that would make every artifact look alike.

Length is still a budget and not a target. You are at 78 lines and have room; if a rule
needs to name a moment, a trigger or an artefact to become executable, spend the words.
Cutting a line that changed none of the five artifacts is worth as much as adding one that
would have.

You are revising, not restarting.

Before you write the file, state in a few lines: for each of the four rules you credited
and that failed, why you now think it did not fire, and what specifically you are changing
about how it is written. Then write the complete revised file to SKILL.md in the current
directory. Output exactly that one file.

Let me analyze the failures carefully.

The four rules I credited that failed:

1. **§8 honesty rules (no fabricated proof)** — The rule said "no invented outcome metrics, no quotes from invented named people or businesses, no client logos, ratings, or customer counts." Yet the builder shipped a testimonial carousel with a named person and a logo wall naming real companies (loom, VERCEL). Why didn't it fire?

Diagnosis: The rule is stated as a *prohibition list* — a principle the builder can agree with while writing copy. At the moment of writing copy, the builder faces the task "fill this section with content" and the prohibition doesn't give it an action; it just forbids a category. Under thinking `low`, the builder pattern-matches "marketing page → testimonial section" and fills it. The rule "no fabricated proof" competes against the much stronger prior of "a landing page has testimonials." The prohibition doesn't tell the builder what to DO at the moment it's deciding the section list. Also "If the brief supplies no proof, there is no testimonial or stats section" — that line exists but it's buried mid-paragraph. It needs to become a decision procedure: before adding any section whose purpose is social proof, check the brief for supplied proof; if absent, omit the section and name the replacement. Make it executable: a section-by-section gate.

Also important: the pricing page invented a logo wall with REAL company names. The rule said "no client logos" but the builder may have considered it "trusted by" styling. The rule needs to name the exact moments: when writing any copy that names a person, company, number, quote, or logo — stop and check whether it came from the brief. Real-company names are worse than invented ones. Need an explicit rule: never name a real company or person as a customer.

2. **Runtime clock (§8)** — The rule said dates come from `new Date()` formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. The prototype typed `Wednesday, May 22`. Why didn't it fire? The rule lives in §8 under "Copy, data, and honesty" — but at the moment the builder wrote the calendar component, it wasn't in "copy writing" mode; it was in "component building" mode. The rule is about a *category* (dates) rather than a *trigger*: the moment you type a date/time string literal into markup. It needs to be reframed as: any time you are about to write a date, weekday, month, or relative-time string into markup, that is a trigger — stop, derive it from the runtime clock. A lint-like self-check: grep the final file for month names, weekday names, "today", etc. That's executable at audit time — the pre-ship audit can include "search the file for weekday/month names and time strings as literals". That's verifiable statically.

3. **Sample data label (§8)** — dashboard lost "Sample data" marker. Why? Same reason: principle, not trigger. The dashboard builder consumed `fixtures/jobs.json` — the very fact that data comes from a fixtures directory is the trigger. Rule should be keyed to the moment: "whenever the data source is a fixture/seed/demo file, the surface carries a visible label." Better: make it part of the build step for data-driven surfaces — the first time you wire data in, decide its provenance label.

4. **Static verification (§10 line "Verification is static: no servers...")** — The builder started `python3 -m http.server` on the "polish and verify" brief. Why didn't it fire? The line is at the very end of the audit section, framed as a description of verification, not as a ban on commands. When the brief says "polish and verify", the builder's prior is "run something to check". The rule needs to be a command-level prohibition stated where the builder will see it when choosing tools: "Do not start servers, open browsers, curl, or screenshot to check your own output unless the brief names that tooling. Verify by re-reading the code." Perhaps move/strengthen: make it an early constraint too, or put it as the first audit line with explicit command examples banned (`python -m http.server`, `npx serve`, `curl localhost`). Naming the exact commands helps a low-thinking model pattern-match at command-composition time.

Also the "polish and verify" trigger: the builder interpreted "verify" as "run a server". So the rule should anticipate: when a brief says "verify/test/check/polish", that word does not authorize tooling; it means re-read the artifact.

5. **Type variety halved** — DM Sans + Manrope on three of four artifacts. The old rule said "two faces max, both loaded" and "display face must have character." Nothing forced variety across artifacts — but wait, these are separate runs, each in an empty directory, no state carried. So the skill cannot coordinate across runs directly; each run independently regressed to the same safe pairing (DM Sans/Manrope are the builder model's priors). How to fix within one file loaded per-run? The rule must attack the *default pairing itself*: name the model's reflex fonts and ban or demote them. E.g., "DM Sans, Inter, Manrope, Poppins, Montserrat are the generated-work tell; pick neither from that list" or require the pairing to be argued from the register with a per-register starting list like the color section has (that worked for grounds!). The color fix worked by giving per-register starting points — do the same for type: per-register pairing suggestions (editorial: Fraunces + Source Serif; technical: Space Grotesk + IBM Plex; brutal: Archivo Black / monospace; warm: ...; luxe-dark: Cormorant + ...). Since each run picks a different register (§1 forces arguing register from subject), per-register type menus will naturally spread the pairings. That's the same mechanism that worked for grounds — argued axis + per-register starting points. Mirror it.

Also ban DM Sans + Manrope specifically? Better: list the "reflex set" — Inter, Roboto, DM Sans, Manrope, Poppins, Montserrat, Open Sans, Lato — and say at most one face from the reflex set, or better: neither face from the reflex set? Hmm, DM Sans can be fine as a quiet text face, but the data shows it's the attractor. The ground fix put "the burden of proof" on the reflex default rather than banning it — that worked. Same here: reflex-set pairings need explicit justification, and each register's starting points name non-reflex fonts. Actually to move the needle harder, I'll say: neither face may come from the reflex list unless the register argument names why. And give concrete per-register pairings with real, reliably-available Google Fonts names.

Per-register font starting points (must be real Google Fonts, reliably available):
- editorial: Fraunces + Newsreader (or Source Serif 4)
- technical: Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono accents
- brutal: Archivo (Black) + Space Mono
- warm-consumer: Fraunces? overlap... maybe "Bricolage Grotesque + Nunito Sans"? Hmm. Warm: "Grenze Gotisch"? Let's pick dependable ones: warm: "Fraunces" is editorial-ish... Use "DM Serif Display"? DM Serif is fine and not in reflex list. warm: DM Serif Display + Work Sans? Work Sans is somewhat reflexy but less. Maybe "Libre Franklin". Let me choose: editorial — Fraunces + Newsreader; technical — Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans; brutal — Archivo Black + Space Mono; warm — DM Serif Display + Libre Franklin; luxe-dark — Cormorant Garamond + Jost? Jost is on Google Fonts, yes. luxe: Cormorant Garamond + Jost; nocturne/instrument: "Fraunces"? no... nocturne: "Sora"? Hmm nocturne was my coined register (deep teal). Pairing: "Syne + Karla"? Syne is on Google Fonts. Or keep six registers and add font pairs: nocturne — Syne + Karla. Those all exist on Google Fonts: Fraunces ✓, Newsreader ✓, Space Grotesk ✓, IBM Plex Sans ✓, Archivo Black ✓, Space Mono ✓, DM Serif Display ✓, Libre Franklin ✓, Cormorant Garamond ✓, Jost ✓, Syne ✓, Karla ✓. Good.

Now, keep line budget ≤150 including frontmatter. Current file is 78 lines. I have room. But every added line must be executable.

Strategy for rewriting the failed rules as triggers/procedures rather than principles:

**Honesty rewrite**: Turn it into a section-gate + a copy-time trigger + an audit grep:
- At section-planning time: "Before adding any section whose job is belief — testimonials, stats band, logo wall, ratings, case study — check the brief for the proof it would display. None supplied → the section does not exist; spend the section on the product instead (a rendered screen, a workflow walk-through)." This is a decision at a named moment (when sketching the section list, which §1 already does).
- At copy-writing time trigger: "About to type a person's name, a company name, a quote, a percentage, or a logo? Its source must be the brief. 'Trusted by' walls are claims: never name a real company or person as a customer, and never invent one."
- Audit: "Read every proper noun and every numeral in the shipped copy: each is from the brief, sample-data-labeled product mock, or runtime-derived. Else delete."

**Clock rewrite**: Trigger phrased at the typing moment: "The moment you are about to type a date, weekday, month, time, or relative label ('today', 'in 2h') into markup or copy — stop. Derive it from `new Date()` with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` at runtime. A hard-coded date is a bug that ships stale." Plus audit: "Search the file for weekday/month names and 'today' as literals in rendered output; each hit must be inside a runtime format call." Hmm, but month names might legitimately appear... e.g., in sample data inside a product mock? If fixture data has dates, formatting them still should use Intl. Static audit: "grep the shipped file for `January|…|December|Monday|…|Sunday` outside of `Intl`/`toLocale` code and fixtures; fix each hit." That's executable statically. Keep it short.

**Sample data rewrite**: key to the data-wiring moment: "When you wire any data source into a surface, classify it at that moment: brief-supplied live data, or fixture/seed/demo/invented. The second kind carries a visible on-surface tag ('Sample data') in the header or summary bar — decided when the data is wired, not at audit time." Plus audit line.

**Server rewrite**: Move it out of the tail of §10 and make it command-shaped: "Verification tooling: the brief did not ask for a server, browser, screenshot, or curl — so you may not start one. 'Verify', 'polish', and 'test' in a brief mean: re-read the shipped code and check it against this audit. Never `python -m http.server`, `npx serve`, `open`, or `curl localhost` to inspect your own output." Naming commands gives the low-thinking builder a pattern to match at command-composition time. Where to put it? It's about working method, maybe near §10 top, or a standalone early line. The failure happened during "polish and verify" — the builder had finished building and chose verification actions. Audit section is fine but it must be imperative and first, not last. I'll make it the opening line of §10.

**Type rewrite**: mirror §4's structure — reflex list with burden of proof + per-register starting pairings. "Reflex faces — Inter, Roboto, DM Sans, Manrope, Poppins, Montserrat, Open Sans — are habits; a pairing drawn from them needs the same justification burden as the paper ground. Starting points per register: editorial Fraunces+Newsreader · technical Space Grotesk+IBM Plex Sans · brutal Archivo Black+Space Mono · warm DM Serif Display+Libre Franklin · luxe Cormorant Garamond+Jost · nocturne Syne+Karla." Wait — DM Serif Display contains "DM" but it's a different family; fine.

Also add to audit: "Pairing not both from the reflex list without an argued reason?"

Now think about why the "kept verbatim" rules generally failed while new rules worked. The prompt suggests: rules that fired (ground axis, contract) were written as *decisions with a named moment and an argument to produce* ("The ground is chosen per artifact from the subject's material world — its lightness and its hue, both argued" and §1 requires naming decisions before coding). - Two faces max, both loaded via `<link>` stylesheet tags from a font CDN. Every family named in CSS must be one actually loaded — never an invented name, never `local()` over a font the machine may lack.
- Reflex faces — Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Poppins, Montserrat, DM Sans, Manrope — are a tell. Using one needs a one-line argument in the §1 comment; otherwise start from the register's pair and adjust: editorial Fraunces + Newsreader · technical Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans · brutal Archivo Black + Space Mono · warm DM Serif Display + Libre Franklin · luxe-dark Cormorant Garamond + Jost · nocturne Syne + Karla.
- The display face must have character (high-contrast serif, wide grotesk, mono); the text face stays quiet.
- `font-feature-settings: "tnum"` and right-aligned figures anywhere numbers appear.

## 4. Color
- Three-color discipline: ground, ink, accent, plus tints of those. Accent covers <10% of pixels — CTAs, one word in a headline, key figures.
- The ground is chosen per artifact from the subject's material world — its lightness and its hue, both argued. Pale neutral ground + near-black ink is the combination that needs justification every time; ship it only when the register's argument says paper. Dark, pure-white, tinted, and saturated grounds are equal citizens — a night-shift tool, a trade business, and a luxury brand must not share one ground.
- Never pure #000 on pure #fff. Paper ≈ #f6f3ec–#faf8f2; ink ≈ #12110e–#1a1a1e; dark grounds ≈ #0d0d0f or a deep chromatic, never navy-purple.
- Starting points per register, not a fixed palette: editorial (paper #f6f3ec, ink #1b1815, oxblood #7c2d2d) · technical (white #ffffff, ink #101014, ultramarine #2b3bff) · brutal (#ffffff, #000000 2px rules, acid #d9ff00) · warm (cream #fbf1e3, espresso #241a10, cherry #e0342f) · luxe-dark (#0e0e10, bone #ece7dd, gold #c9a227) · nocturne (deep teal #0d2925, mist #dcebe4, signal #ff5a3c). The grounds span paper → white → cream → near-black → deep color on purpose; that spread is the point.

## 5. Layout
- Required per page: at least one full-bleed band, one element that overlaps a boundary or breaks the grid, one asymmetric split (e.g. 5/7 columns). All-centered alignment is a failure.
- Alternate section surfaces for rhythm (light → dark → light, or ground → tint). Five identical sections is a failure.
- Vary container widths (mix full-bleed, ~1280px, ~640px measures) and vertical padding (96–160px, different per section). Let one section be mostly whitespace.
- Separate with 1px hairlines at 10–15% ink opacity, not shadows. Shadows only on genuinely floating elements, large and soft: `0 24px 48px -12px rgb(0 0 0 / .18)`.
- Build "imagery" in code — SVG diagrams, generative canvas, charts, rendered mini-UI of the product — never empty placeholder boxes.

## 6. Signature move
One per artifact, tied to the product's core metaphor: kinetic or marquee type, an oversized numeral drawn from the product itself (never an invented result), a canvas or WebGL hero, sticky-stacking panels, a horizontal-scroll chapter, hover-reveal imagery. Execute it fully and keep everything around it quiet. It usually lives in the hero; if not, the hero must be oversized typography doing the talking or the product itself rendered live — never a text stack.

## 7. Motion
- Entrances 600–900ms, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, stagger children 50–90ms, animate transform/opacity only. Micro-interactions 150–250ms.
- Every interactive element gets a hover state that moves something — translate, underline draw, arrow nudge, color invert — not a bare opacity dip. Style `:focus-visible` in the accent.
- Choreograph the hero on load; do not make scroll-reveal the only trick. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## 8. Copy, data, and honesty
- Invent a plausible brand name and voice. Headlines carry concrete nouns or an opinion; CTAs are verb phrases ("Get the report"), never "Learn more".
- **Evidence trigger**: the moment you are about to type a person's name, a company name, a quote, a numeral presented as fact, or a logo into copy — stop and name its source. "The brief", or it does not ship. That bans invented testimonials, invented metrics, ratings, and customer counts — and, worst of all, naming real companies or people as customers of a product that has none. When proof is absent, concreteness comes from the product: what it does, what its screen shows, how the day runs with it.
- Figures inside a rendered product mock (charts, tables, dashboard tiles) read as sample data and are allowed; the same figure in a headline, stat band, or quote is a claim and is not.
- **Provenance is decided when you wire the data, not at audit**: brief-supplied live data ships plain; fixture, seed, demo, or invented data carries a visible "Sample data" tag in that surface's header or summary bar. A surface that feels live also shows its reference instant ("Updated 14:32") derived from the runtime clock.
- **Clock trigger**: the moment you are about to type a date, weekday, month, time, or relative label ("today", "in 2h") into anything rendered — stop. Derive it from `new Date()` with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, including values that arrive as strings in fixtures. A typed date ships stale and is often already wrong, weekdays especially.
- Set `::selection` to the accent. Ship an inline SVG favicon. For paper and luxe registers, lay 3–5% opacity SVG-noise grain over the surface.
- The footer is a canvas — oversized wordmark or wordmark-as-graphic — not a four-column link farm.
- Dashboards: density is the aesthetic. Hairline grid, tabular right-aligned figures, one excellent chart beats five placeholder cards.

## 9. Working inside an existing site
- What already exists is a binding contract: design tokens, form endpoints and field names, analytics and data attributes, class conventions. Extend within them; replace or rename none.
- Add no new files to the delivered site's own directory. Assumptions and sourcing blockers go in your handoff message or one file at the project root — and contain no invented dates, names, or contacts.

## 10. Pre-ship audit — static only; re-read the built code and fix every "no"
- "Verify", "polish", or "test" in a brief authorizes no tooling. Do not start servers (`python -m http.server`, `npx serve`), open browsers, screenshot, or `curl` your own output unless the brief explicitly names that tool. Verification is re-reading the shipped code against this list.
- §1 comment present, and the page actually looks like it? Ground argued per §4, not the reflex paper-and-near-black? Every belief section backed by supplied proof (§1)?
- Evidence sweep: read every proper noun, quote, and numeral-as-fact in the copy — each traces to the brief, a labeled product mock, or the runtime. Fixture-backed surfaces show "Sample data" and a clock-derived reference instant?
- String sweep: re-read for typed weekday/month names, dates, times, and "today" in rendered output — each must be produced by a runtime format call, never typed.
- Display type ≥ 4× body? Exactly one accent? At least one broken-grid or overlap moment? Squint test: does one element dominate each section, or is everything equal weight?
- Both font families really `<link>`-loaded and referenced under their own names? Pairing argued, not reflex (§3)?
- Every clickable has a hover that moves something and a `:focus-visible` state? One `<h1>`, no skipped heading levels; `<button>` for actions, `<a>` for navigation; every input labeled; decorative SVG/canvas `aria-hidden`, informative ones named?
- Contrast computed, not eyeballed: body and label text ≥ 4.5:1 against its actual ground — accent-colored text and text on tinted bands first.
- Every interactive target ≥ 44×44px? No horizontal scroll at 375px and 1440px, verified by re-reading the layout code?
- Zero banned patterns from §2?
